reference:
Uncle Alp made sure everything was comfortable for Heidi. He made a new
chair tall enough for her to reach the table.
In the afternoon, Peter came to return Uncle Alp's goats.
The next morning, Uncle Alp told Heidi, "Go with Peter and he will
introduce you to this area."
They chatted about the goats Peter was herding. When Heidi found that
the goat who had lost her mother looked sad, she hugged the poor goat and
promised to keep her company.
Suddenly, Peter stood up and rushed to grab the leg of a small goat that was
about to fall into the deep hole.
"Heidi, come and help me save Finch!" he barked.
Heidi turned to her grandfather and asked, "When can I go outside,
Grandfather?"
Grandfather looked at the deep snow and replied, "Not now, Heidi. The
snow is too deep. But you can go soon."
Day after day, Heidi would ask, "Grandfather, is today the day we can visit
Grannie?"
And then one day, Grandfather smiled at her and said, "Yes, Heidi. Today,
we can go see Grannie." With excitement, they got on their sleds and slid down
the mountain to Grannie's little hut.
